newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Long end leads a mixed day.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Long end leads a mixed day.

text.p: The Australian bond market put in a mixed performance against other dollar-bloc bond markets on Wednesday, seeing some morning gains eroded through the afternoon session when yields eased to their lows.
Spreads ended roughly unchanged at the short end, although the long end did manage to hold onto some gains, a performance which also saw the local yield curve flatten.
Traders saw the day as one of consolidation after the gains since the end of March, when the spread to U.S. 10-year bonds was over 140 points.

Trade was lacklustre as the market waits for direction from labour force data on Thursday, and so bonds did not really have the impetus to continue there narrowing of the past week, although the spread to U.S. 10-year Treasuries was under 110 basis points around the middle of the day.
Forecasts for the March labour force data centre on a rise of 13,500 and an unemployment rate of 8.7 percent.
In February, employment fell 7,200 and the unemployment rate was 8.8 percent.

Treasuries are expected to retain their bearish underlying tone on Wednesday, despite no data being released, with the market concerned about U.S. rates and the prospect of higher than expected inflation data next week.
